batch_geocode.description: Geocode many addresses at once: a spreadsheet column, a list of branches, the results of an earlier step. Every address given comes back in the order it was sent, matched or not, each beside the text it was looked up under, and the counts say how many matched. Far cheaper and faster than geocoding each address in a loop.

geocode_address.description: Turn an address, postcode or place name into latitude and longitude, plus a cleaned-up standard address and every layer around it: street, neighborhood, city, postcode, region and country, each as its own field. Use it to put a spreadsheet of addresses on a map, to normalise addresses typed by hand, or to get the coordinates the routing actions need.

get_directions.description: Route between two points, optionally through stops on the way. Returns the distance, the travel time, turn-by-turn instructions, and a leg-by-leg breakdown between stops. Driving routes use live traffic by default, and can be asked for a departure or arrival time to get a prediction for then instead of now.
get_directions.name: get_directions

parameters.description: Where the route starts, written as "latitude,longitude", for example "37.7749,-122.4194". Use "Geocode an address" first to turn an address into a point.
parameters.name: origin

parameters.description: Where the route ends, written as "latitude,longitude".
parameters.name: destination

parameters.description: Points to visit between the start and the end, in the order given, each written as "latitude,longitude". Leave empty for a direct route. Up to 23.
parameters.name: waypoints

parameters.description: How the trip is made. Driving with live traffic gives the most accurate time for a trip starting now.
parameters.name: profile

parameters.description: Road types to keep off the route. Driving only: ignored for walking and cycling. Best effort: Mapbox will still use one if it is the only way through.
parameters.name: avoid

parameters.description: Leave at this time instead of now, and get the travel time predicted for then. Driving only. Cannot be combined with an arrival time.
parameters.name: depart_at

parameters.description: Work backwards from arriving at this time. Driving only, and it switches off live traffic because Mapbox answers arrival-time routes from historical data. Cannot be combined with a departure time.
parameters.name: arrive_by

parameters.description: Return each instruction along the route. Turn off for a smaller result when only the distance and time are needed.
parameters.name: include_steps

parameters.description: Also return up to two other routes that are close in time but meaningfully different. They may not exist.
parameters.name: alternatives

parameters.description: The language for the turn-by-turn instructions. Defaults to English.
parameters.name: language

alternative_routes.description: Other routes, when they were asked for.

duration_typical_seconds.description: Travel time under typical conditions, ignoring today's traffic. Driving with traffic only.

geometry.description: The route line as an encoded polyline (precision 5).

profile.description: The travel mode the route was built for.

reason.description: Why no route was found, when there wasn't one.

waypoints.description: Each given point as Mapbox snapped it to a road.

get_reachable_area.description: The area you can reach from a point within a set travel time: an isochrone. Use it to draw a delivery or service zone, to show a 15-minute walk from a shop, or as a catchment to test addresses against. Returns one outline per travel time asked for, largest first, as GeoJSON polygons ready to draw on a map.
get_reachable_area.display_name: Get the area reachable in a given time
get_reachable_area.display_str_template: Get the area reachable from {0} with Mapbox.
get_reachable_area.name: get_reachable_area

parameters.description: The point to measure out from, written as "latitude,longitude".
parameters.name: center

parameters.description: How far out to draw, in travel time. Choose up to four; each becomes its own outline.
parameters.name: minutes

parameters.description: How the travel is done.
parameters.name: profile

parameters.description: Road types to keep out of the area. Driving only: ignored for walking and cycling.
parameters.name: avoid

parameters.description: Draw the area for leaving at this time rather than now, so it reflects the traffic expected then. Driving only.

geojson.description: Mapbox's whole GeoJSON FeatureCollection, to hand straight to a mapping tool.

minutes_requested.description: The travel times asked for, in ascending order.

get_travel_time_matrix.description: Travel time and distance from every origin to every destination, in one request. This is what answers 'which of our depots is closest to each customer', 'which technician should take this job', or 'which of these flats are within 20 minutes of the office'. Results come back both as a grid and as one row per pair, which is the form a filter or a sort can read. Leave the destinations empty to measure every point against every other.
get_travel_time_matrix.display_name: Get travel times between many points
get_travel_time_matrix.display_str_template: Get Mapbox travel times between points.
get_travel_time_matrix.name: get_travel_time_matrix

parameters.description: The points to measure from, each written as "latitude,longitude".
parameters.name: origins

parameters.description: The points to measure to, each written as "latitude,longitude". Leave empty to measure every origin against every other origin.
parameters.name: destinations

parameters.description: How the trips are made. Driving with live traffic is limited to 10 points in total; the others allow 25.

parameters.description: What to return for each pair of points.

destination_count.description: How many points were measured to.

destinations.description: Each destination as snapped to a road.

distances_meters.description: Distances in meters as a grid, laid out the same way. Empty unless distances were asked for.

durations_seconds.description: Travel times in seconds as a grid: row i, column j is origin i to destination j. Null where there is no route.

origin_count.description: How many points were measured from.

origins.description: Each origin as Mapbox snapped it to a road.

pairs.description: The same numbers as one row per origin/destination pair, the form to filter or sort on.

reason.description: Why no matrix was returned, when there wasn't one.

optimize_route.description: Given a set of stops, work out the quickest order to visit them all: the travelling-salesman problem, solved. This is what turns an unordered list of deliveries, service calls or viewings into a route sheet. Returns the stops in visiting order along with the total distance and time. Up to 12 stops.

optimize_route.display_str_template: Put stops in the fastest order with Mapbox.
optimize_route.name: optimize_route

search_places.description: Search for businesses, landmarks and addresses by name: "Blue Bottle Coffee", "Heathrow Terminal 5", "pharmacy". Returns each place's coordinates, full address, categories, phone number, website and opening hours. Set 'Near' to search somewhere specific; without it Mapbox guesses from where the request came from, which for a workflow is a data centre.
